next_question: Can a fully-ambiguous content mapping (all 3 states share 1 content hash, eliminating partial state discrimination) with stochastic branching FSM yield conditional PMI > 0.05 bits at K=3, resolving whether the residual 0.226 bits from EXP-PHYSICS-35137030850 reflects genuine predictive dynamics beyond aliasing or is entirely explained by partial state discrimination?
why_next: EXP-PHYSICS-35137030850 demonstrates BC PMI=0.226 bits persists with many-to-one content mapping (S0/S1 share hash, S2 unique), but audit V4 identifies a critical confound: the 2-hash many-to-one condition still permits partial state discrimination (S2 isolated from {S0,S1}), so the residual PMI cannot distinguish genuine predictive dynamics from partial aliasing. A fully-ambiguous (1-hash) condition where ALL states share the same content hash would eliminate partial discrimination entirely. If PMI>0 persists with 1 hash, it demonstrates genuine response-context dynamics. If PMI→0, the signal was entirely from partial state discrimination. This is the minimal next experiment to resolve the dominant unknown. It is low-cost (same FSM, only content mapping changes) and directly resolves V4. After this, the Physics lane should pivot to production SPA infrastructure where the synthetic-to-real gap is the dominant bottleneck.

established: BC PMI persists with many-to-one content mapping: 0.226 bits (Bonferroni p=0.0 < 0.0125, H=1.533 bits) on 3-state stochastic branching FSM where S0 and S1 share content hash (2 unique hashes) and S2 is unique. Content-state aliasing is a significant (54% reduction from unique-content 0.493 bits) but not sole source of PMI.

Bias-corrected MI estimator validated on stochastic branching FSM: positive control (content-shuffled BC PMI=0.002 ≈ 0 on H>0 strata) and null control (shuffled labels BC mean=0.0, std=0.0068) both pass. Finite-sample bias ~0.05 bits (perm_mean for MTO K3=0.052) correctly removed by BC correction.

Stochastic branching FSM eliminates ceiling: H(S_next|URL,H_K=3)=1.533 bits (MTO) / 1.537 bits (UNIQ), both >> 0.2 threshold. Session-direction stochasticity (p_left=0.7, p_right=0.3) creates genuine non-determinism verified by transition probability estimates.

Determinism check passes with step grouping on both conditions: P(Response_hash|FSM_state,session,step)=1.0 (MTO 571 groups, UNIQ 582 groups, 0 violations). Content is deterministic per (state, session, step) as designed.
Unique-content baseline within-experiment: BC PMI=0.493 bits at K=3 with identical FSM/sessions, 3 unique hashes. The 0.268-bit difference quantifies aliasing contribution.
rejected: Content-state aliasing as sole source of PMI is rejected: many-to-one BC PMI=0.226 > 0 (not ≈ 0), demonstrating PMI persists when content is ambiguous for 2 of 3 states. Frozen falsifier clause 2 ('aliasing was sole source') is not supported by the evidence.

The frozen rule's FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING verdict is arithmetically correct (C3: diff -0.268 < -0.1) but the interpretation 'PMI vanishes with many-to-one mapping' is not justified — the evidence shows 45.8% of unique-content signal survives.
unknown: Whether the residual 0.226 bits reflects genuine response-context dynamics (structural information in ambiguous content about transition probabilities) or entirely from partial state discrimination (S2 unique hash isolates S2 from {S0,S1}). Requires fully-ambiguous 1-hash condition.
Whether PMI>0 would persist with fully-ambiguous content mapping (all 3 states share 1 hash, 0 partial discrimination). This is the critical test to resolve V4.
Whether the 54% PMI reduction from unique-to-many-to-one generalizes to other FSM topologies, state counts (5, 10 states), and transition structures (Markov, hidden state).
Whether the PMI pipeline detects similar structure on production SPAs with stochastic transitions, client-side rendering, auth-dependent content, and external data feeds (synthetic-to-real gap).
do_not_assume: Do not assume the FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING verdict means PMI=0 — the evidence shows PMI>0 persists (0.226 bits, p_bonf=0.0). The frozen rule's C3 threshold (diff > -0.1) triggers on significant-but-not-sole aliasing, not on absence of signal.

Do not interpret residual 0.226 bits as validated evidence for 'genuine predictive dynamics beyond aliasing' — partial discrimination confound (audit V4) means the signal could be entirely from S2 isolation. The 1-hash test is required.

Do not generalize beyond this synthetic 3-state stochastic branching FSM with hash-based SHA-256 observation on locally-hosted Express server. Production SPAs have client-side rendering, auth-dependent content, stochastic external data, and richer DOM/accessibility representations.

Do not assume the PMI pipeline is validated for production use — all tests are synthetic with known structure; no experiment has demonstrated PMI detection on genuinely stochastic real-web transitions.

Do not assume the C3 threshold (diff > -0.1) is scientifically meaningful as a falsifier — audit V3 identifies it as conceptually misaligned with the 'sole source' falsifier clause in spec.json falsifier clause 2.

Do not assume action-sequence non-identity across conditions (audit V9: RNG advances sequentially, so action sequences differ between MTO and UNIQ despite identical session_directions) biases the difference estimate materially — both conditions have 2000 transitions and stochastic noise unlikely to shift 0.268-bit difference.

Do not treat this experiment as closing C-WEB-DYNAMICS — the hypothesis concerns real Web dynamics and remains untested on production SPAs with stochastic transitions, client-side rendering, auth-dependent content, or external data feeds.
